paraphrase: The single-practice samādhi (ekavyūha-samādhi): one who, in a quiet place, sits facing the direction of a buddha, fixes the mind on that one buddha and recites his name without break, sees in that one buddha all buddhas of past, present and future, and knows the sameness of the dharmadhātu.
notes: Reference from the unit author's knowledge at chapter level; passage not read in a local text in this phase. Cited by Daoxin of the Chan East Mountain school.
